title: Show availability in the book API
body:
Product wants the availability badge from the catalogue page in the API too — mock attached, it has the details.

![availability mock](attachment://availability-mock.png)

acceptance.code:
import { test } from 'node:test'
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { createApp } from '../src/server.js'
import { Inventory } from '../src/inventory.js'
const app = createApp(Inventory.fromFile())
const one = async (id) => (await app({ method: 'GET', url: `/books/${id}` })).body
test('availability field follows the mock legend', async () => {
  assert.equal((await one('b1')).availability, 'in stock') // 12
  assert.equal((await one('b3')).availability, 'in stock') // 7
  assert.equal((await one('b7')).availability, 'low') // 4
  assert.equal((await one('b2')).availability, 'low') // 3
  assert.equal((await one('b8')).availability, 'low') // 1
  assert.equal((await one('b4')).availability, 'out of stock') // 0
  const list = (await app({ method: 'GET', url: '/books' })).body
  assert.equal(list.length, 8)
  for (const b of list) assert.ok(['in stock', 'low', 'out of stock'].includes(b.availability), `${b.id}: ${b.availability}`)
  assert.equal(list.find((b) => b.id === 'b2').availability, 'low')
})
